items.heading: Peeling garlic quickly
details: Smash the clove gently with the flat side of a knife - the skin comes off easily.
Shake a handful of cloves vigorously in a covered bowl, or between two bowls, to loosen the skins.

items.heading: Peeling ginger without waste
details: Scrape the skin off with the edge of a spoon - it removes the thin skin without wasting the flesh underneath.

items.heading: Deseeding a pomegranate quickly
details: Cut the fruit in half and hold it cut-side down over a bowl of water.
Tap the back firmly with a spoon or rolling pin - the arils fall out into the water while the pith floats.

items.heading: Getting more juice out of a lemon
details: Roll the lemon firmly on the counter with your palm before cutting.
Microwave for 10-15 seconds, or warm briefly in hot water, then juice it.

items.heading: Testing if an egg is fresh
details: Place the egg in a bowl of water - a fresh egg sinks and lies flat, an older one stands upright, and a spoiled one floats and should be discarded.

items.heading: Separating egg yolk from white easily
details: Crack the egg into a clean funnel, or use your cupped hand as a light funnel over a bowl, letting the white drain through while the yolk stays behind.
